card.title: Magnetic field and magnetic force on moving charges

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A moving charge feels q v B sinθ, perpendicular to its velocity, so the speed stays constant. Perpendicular motion is a circle of radius m v /(q B). Motion along the field feels no magnetic force, and a general velocity makes a helix.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
F = qvB sinθ
ε = −N dΦ/dt
F = BIL

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The proton mass is 1.67 × 10^−27 kg.  ·  e = 1.6 × 10^−19 C.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: A charge moving in a magnetic field feels a force q v B sinθ. θ is the angle between the velocity and the field. The force is zero if the charge is at rest or if it moves parallel to the field.  ·  The force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the field. A positive charge follows the right-hand rule. A negative charge is pushed the opposite way.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Magnetic force  ·  No work  ·  Cyclotron radius  ·  Helix

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: No force if the charge is at rest.  ·  The force is perpendicular to v.  ·  Speed does not change.  ·  Perpendicular motion is a circle.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Force on moving charge F = q(v×B); on a wire F = BIL sinθ.  ·  Faraday: EMF ε = −dΦ/dt; Lenz's law gives the sign (induced current opposes the change in flux).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Why is the kinetic energy constant?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A proton moves at 2.0 × 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a 0.10 T field. Take q = 1.6 × 10^−19 C and m = 1.67 × 10^−27 kg. Find the force and the radius.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: A charge at rest in a magnetic field feels → B  ·  The magnetic force changes → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Because the force is always perpendicular to the velocity, it does no work. The speed stays constant. Only the direction changes.  ·  If the velocity is perpendicular to a uniform field, the path is a circle. The radius is m v / (q B). A faster charge, or a heavier one, makes a larger circle. A stronger field makes a tighter circle.  ·  If the velocity has a component along the field, that component is not changed and the path is a helix. The pitch is set by the parallel speed and the time to go once around.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: L = NΦ/I  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ force on moving charge f = q(v×b); on a wire f = bil sinθ..  ·  A stationary charge feels no magnetic force.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The magnetic force does not increase the speed.  ·  sinθ is 1 only for perpendicular motion.  ·  Negative charges curve the other way.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Use the perpendicular component of velocity.  ·  State the sign of the charge before the direction of the curve.  ·  Write F = q v B sinθ and say what each symbol means.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  Limit to remember: force on moving charge f = q(v×b); on a wire f = bil sinθ.  ·  The tesla is the field in which a charge of 1 C moving at 1 m/s perpendicular to the field feels a force of 1 N. Laboratory fields of a fraction of a tesla already bend electron beams.
